scope: Counter-battery original observer-session continuity from delayed server wake through owner scan and server fire admission. Not new detection capability or physical acceptance.
defect: The server delay retained its generation, but its observer message omitted it. The owner created a new fifteen-second deadline on receipt and queued scan callbacks checked enabled state only. A delayed wake, unfinished scan or delayed remote fire reply could cross disable/re-enable into a later counter-battery generation.
implementation: Server wake carries original generation and dispatch-time fifteen-second deadline. Delivery consumes, rather than renews, that deadline. Invalid, expired or different-generation envelopes refuse.
Every existing four-observer callback checks the retained generation and deadline; original generation accompanies its remote fire request.

Server fire admission requires a finite integral matching generation for remote COUNTER requests before selecting/reserving a battery. Direct local server scripts may omit it. Radar internal requests explicitly carry their captured generation as well.
No observation position oracle, new observer roster, scan, timer or movement command. Native knowledge, visibility, transmit, owner and feature gates remain unchanged.

validation.focused: 4 existing counter-battery lifecycle cases passed with extended wake/queue/reply source contracts; test count unchanged. These are static contracts, not a multiplayer simulation.

limits: Actual network ordering, setting toggles, HC ownership and live-fire behaviour remain unverified; audits paused.
A receiver may conservatively refuse when public generation delivery lags the request; there is no replay that renews the window.
Does not retract issued native fire or projectiles; existing mission/shot generation fences still own later cancellation.
Full required controller handovers, overall source parity and5%median/10%p95 performance remain incomplete.
